audits.mathematicalReason: The original surface area is 6 × 3² = 54 cm². Removing a unit corner cube removes three exposed unit faces and exposes three previously internal unit faces, giving zero net change. The eight original corner cubes do not share faces, so this cancellation remains valid throughout their removal. Surface-area invariance is therefore a valid selected method, supported by the cube surface-area formula; direct face counting would also be possible.

audits.mathematicalReason: Folding P onto R uses diagonal QS as the crease and halves the square's footprint. Folding Q onto S then uses the other diagonal, PR, and halves the resulting isosceles right triangle's footprint. Thus the final area is one quarter of the original square's area. The original area is 4 × 9 = 36 in², its positive side length is √36 = 6 inches, and its perimeter is 4 × 6 = 24 inches. The folding, reflection, square-area, square-root, and perimeter scopes are defensible in their proposed roles.

audits.mathematicalReason: There are nine equally likely ordered outcome pairs. A product is odd exactly when both labels are odd: the first spinner has two odd labels and the second has one. Hence P(odd product) = (2/3)(1/3) = 2/9, and P(even product) = 1 − 2/9 = 7/9. Equivalently, enumeration gives seven favorable pairs out of nine. Both listed routes are valid alternatives; their techniques need not be combined in one solution.
